packageRules.description: Markdown tooling moves together: prettier, markdownlint, and cspell gate the same checks, so review them in one PR.
Action digest bumps are mechanical and the workflows re-run on the PR, so they need no staged rollout.

templates/Directory.Packages.props and templates/global.json are CONTENT, not this repository's dependencies: nothing builds against them. The refresh-dotnet-versions skill maintains them. It resolves each pin against nuget.org, checks target-framework compatibility, reads release notes on a major bump, and updates the 'verified on <date>' header comment. A bot that bumps only the version string leaves the header wrong, and audit-freshness can then no longer tell a reviewed pin from an unreviewed one. Scoped to templates/, not nuget as a whole, because the #:package pins under scripts/ are real dependencies: the checks compile against YamlDotNet, and bumping it is the mechanical change Renovate exists for.

The SDK pin in a global.json is a floor, not a selection: rollForward latestFeature already takes the newest feature band and patch installed on the machine. Every bump Renovate can offer either narrows that floor to a patch, failing contributors one servicing release behind for nothing, or names a band latestFeature would have accepted anyway. The one edit that is real is a major bump, which latestFeature does not cross, and that arrives through the dotnet-release-watch workflow and refresh-dotnet-versions. Renovate's nuget manager reads global.json and defaults rangeStrategy to bump, so without this it would raise the floor to an exact patch build. Matched by depType so it covers the root and templates/ files alike.

nuget.description: The scripts/ checks are .NET 10 file-based apps that declare their packages with #:package. Renovate understands the directive but does not scan .cs by default, so YamlDotNet would sit unbumped without this. Patterns are added to the manager defaults, not substituted for them, and scoping to scripts/ keeps the example and generated .cs files under templates/ out of it.
